summary: Ryosho Nakamura is a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied at Seventh Higher School, Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, and Rissho University. He served as a professor at Kagoshima International University from circa 1967 to 1998.

Ryosho Tanaka (1933–2016) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar educated at Komazawa University. He held multiple roles at Komazawa University, including professor (1964), dean (1991), and president (2009), and was also a professor at Ryukoku University.

Ryoshu Kouda specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Seitatsu Matsunami. Kouda's career includes researcher posts attested at Taisho University in 1998 and the Hasegawa Buddhist Cultural Institute in 2006.

Ryoshu Michihata (1903–1993) worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. After studying at Otani University from circa 1923 to 1928, he held a post there from circa 1934 to 1973 and was a professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University in 1976.
Ryoshu Misaki (1921–2010) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University from circa 1941 to 1944. He later served as professor emeritus at Waseda University from circa 1967 to 1992.

Ryoshun Okubo specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology and studied at Waseda University (circa 1973–1983). He became Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism at Waseda University circa 2003, with faculty posts attested at ICPBS and IIBS in 2026.

Ryosuke Furui is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who earned his PhD at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2007. He has held positions at the University of Tokyo, attested in 2011 and as professor in 2020.
Ryota Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Toyo University (attested 2015). In 2015, he held researcher posts at Toyo University and the Shinran Buddhist Center.
Ryotai Shibuya was a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who completed studies at Tendai Sect University and Kokugakuin University.

Ryoun Yamada is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Harvard Business School. He worked at Mitsubishi Bank from circa 1962 to 1996 among several corporate appointments, and became leader of Sanbo Zen in 2004.

Ryudo Fujii specializes in Indology and philosophy, having studied under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson. His career includes posts at the JSPS (attested 2003), Kokushikan University (attested 2010), and Kyoto Women's University (attested 2015).
Ryudo Suita is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held an appointment as a lecturer at Bukkyo University, attested from 1997 to 2010, with affiliation attested there again in 2020.

Ryugen Taga is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (circa 1953–1955). He served at Rissho University as a lecturer (1961), associate professor (1972), professor (circa 1975–2001), and president (1993).

Ryugen Tanemura works in Buddhist studies and Indology. His appointments include positions at Nishogakusha University (attested 2013), Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014), and Taisho University (attested 2014–2026).

Ryuichi Abe specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, educated at Keio, Johns Hopkins, and Columbia under Yoshito S. Hakeda and Philip Boas Yampolsky. He taught at Columbia (1991–2004) and became a professor at Harvard circa 2006.

Ryujo Yamada (1895–1974) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied under Sylvain Lévi. He was a professor at Tohoku University (attested 1953) and served as head of Musashino University (attested 1963).

Ryuken Nawa is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. In records attested for 2026, Nawa holds appointments as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Ryuken Sato (1930–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar attested in 2014 as an emeritus professor at Taisho University and an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute.
Ryuo (1856–1926) was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Tō-ji (as Sōgaku) and also held a teaching post at Koyasan University.
Ryusei Keira is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who completed a thesis at the University of Lausanne in 2003 under the doctoral supervision of Tom Tillemans.
